newsitem.title: USA: Video holder to make $6/shr bid for co.
newsitem.headline: Video holder to make $6/shr bid for co.

text.p: A major shareholder of Video Lottery Technologies Inc, William Spier, said on Friday he filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission his intention to form an investment group to offer to buy the company for $6 per share in cash.
Video, which provides terminals, software and services to the video lottery market, closed at 4-1/2 Friday, up 49/64.
With about 10.7 million shares outstanding, the Spier bid is worth about $64.2 million.
Spier said in a letter addressed to the company's board of directors that the cash price represents about a 90 percent premium over current stock market prices.
He requested a response from Video Lottery by November 25.
No one was immediately available at Video Lottery to comment on the bid.
Spier also said he would recommend the company "shop" itself around for a higher bidder in the period between signing an agreement with Spier through December 31, 1996.

"Indeed, we consider this price so attractive that, if VLT could obtain an equal or superior cash proposal for all outstanding shares, we, as one of the largest shareholders in VLT, would support that proposal," Spier said in the letter.

A former co-chairman of Salomon Bros who retired in 1982, Spier said the offer is friendly and that he was not interested in making a hostile bid. He said he owns about 2.5 percent of Video Lottery shares.
"Given the company's situation, we believe it is in everyone's interest to determine the company's future quickly," the letter said.
